supporting_observations.claim: From 13:41:40 through 14:06:35 UTC, WS-EBROOKS-01 made six outbound proxy CONNECT attempts to update.stockpilot.co, spaced approximately five minutes apart; the first returned 502 and subsequent attempts returned 200.

Endpoint network records attribute these connections to PID 6464, C:\Users\eli.brooks\AppData\Local\StockPilot\stockpilotupd.exe, running as eli.brooks. This differs from the inventoried approved updater location, C:\Program Files\StockPilot\stockpilotupd.exe.
The updater process was created with a Chrome parent, and a file-creation event for the updater executable was recorded shortly afterward.

The observed destination is update.stockpilot.co, whereas the inventory identifies update.stockpilot.com as the approved StockPilot update domain. Together with the unexpected executable location and process provenance, this supports treating the periodic activity as malicious rather than as the approved updater.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations and outcomes, but the supplied evidence does not include TLS certificates, full request or response content, or the remote server's resolved IP.
The evidence does not provide the executable's hash, signature, download source, or a forensic copy for analysis.
The proxy user-agent labels the connections as Edge, while endpoint network events attribute them to the StockPilot updater process; the supplied records do not explain this discrepancy.
claims_not_established: The identity, ownership, or malicious infrastructure status of update.stockpilot.co is not established by these records alone.
The contents or purpose of the outbound HTTPS exchanges, and whether any data was sent or received beyond the logged connection metadata, are not established.
The evidence does not establish who created or installed the executable, or whether the Chrome parent reflects a user action, a download, or another mechanism.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and analyze the updater executable; obtain its hash, signature, provenance, and any related download or browser history.
Review proxy and DNS records for the destination, including resolved IPs, TLS certificate details, and any available request or response metadata.
Check for the same executable, destination domain, or related activity on other hosts and accounts.
unrelated_findings: Separate investigation: DC-BLU-01 records a Kerberos ticket request for ken.ito from WS-EBROOKS-01's address, followed by a logon to WS-KITO-01 from that address. Inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-KITO-01; these records do not establish whether this activity is related to the alert. (T215-00096–T215-00099)

Separate investigation: ruth.moss launched msra.exe targeting WS-EBROOKS-01 and supplied eli.brooks credentials. Inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-KITO-01; the provided records do not establish that a remote session succeeded or that this is related to the alert. (T215-00186–T215-00188)
